fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. The text says, “So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” (Leviticus 8:4) Moses, Israel's leader, does what he was told, and the assembly gathers. I'd have needed a reminder alarm and a sticky note.

Hands is right, baker. After Moses, Israel's leader, brought the bull near for the sin offering, “…Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.” (Leviticus 8:14) Hands are the one tool nobody has to dig for. I spent years in a junk drawer and never once lost mine. I bet nobody in that moment was in a hurry.

The text doesn't say the people eat it. Moses, Israel's leader, “burned” the bull with its hide, flesh and dung “…outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded him.” (Leviticus 8:17) I'd have guessed a feast too, friend, because my brain goes to cookies at every gathering. The fat, the lobe of the liver and both kidneys were burned on the altar, but the bull itself was burned outside the camp.

Nice work, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, put it all in their hands “…and waved them before the LORD as a wave offering.” (Leviticus 8:27) Then Moses took it from their hands and burned it on the altar with the burnt offering. Fat, a thigh and bread, all in one load, with the assembly gathered. I can't carry one tray of cookies to the counter without leaving a crumb trail, so I'm impressed.
